clue.text: Town's MP ran, tho' unfortunately not returned

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: tho' is the clipped form of though; its letters THO join the mix

indicators.note: returned means the word not is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: An election report: the local MP stood, but sadly the voters did not return him to Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' scrambles MP, RAN and THO into NORTHAMP; 'returned' turns NOT into TON. 'returned' plays on an MP being returned at an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Northampton is a large county town in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Skull parts found unexpectedly in BP's ice location

indicators.note: turning up unexpectedly suggests letters arriving in a surprising order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bones turn up at an oil company's frozen drilling site, a grisly discovery for BP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges all fourteen letters of BPSICELOCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: The occipital bones form the back and base of the cranium, so they are parts of a skull.

clue.text: Excessively tense to play the flute

parts.note: excessively means too much, too
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A flautist is too nervous to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: To toot is to sound a wind instrument with short blasts, a playful way of describing flute playing.

clue.text: Liberal line adopted by pliant duenna is set aside

indicators.note: something adopted by another is taken into it, so these letters go inside
pliant means bendable, so the letters of duenna are bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: A compliant chaperone takes in a Liberal policy and has it overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pliant' rearranges DUENNA as ANNUED, and 'adopted by' puts LL inside it. 'is' is a link word; a duenna is a Spanish chaperone.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a ruling or marriage is to cancel it or set it aside as void.

clue.text: See 18
Party's web organisation having suggestion of yuppiedom

parts.note: .org is the web domain for organisations

indicators.note: a mere suggestion of a word is just a hint of it, its first letter

explanation.surface: A political party's website organisation hints at a yuppie lifestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild, debauched party.

clue.text: An optimistic point?

parts.note: a point is a cape or headland, and an optimistic one would be full of good hope

explanation.surface: An upbeat argument made in a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like a point in an argument, but it is a headland; the southern African cape famously carries an optimistic name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a point of land, and this one at the tip of Africa is named for good hope.

clue.text: Street name I confused for hours in New York?

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tourist muddles a street name while working out what time it is in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges STREETNAMEI; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: New York keeps the time zone of the eastern United States, so its clock hours are on that time.

clue.text: A Catholic noble, popular leader of group, a tad devious providing necessary financial information

parts.note: a count is a nobleman
in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
devious means winding or crooked, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: A shady Catholic aristocrat and a crowd-pleasing group leader hand over the figures the auditors need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' rearranges A TAD as DATA; 'providing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounting data are the figures a business records and reports about its finances.

clue.text: Parliament has divergent ways for landing in appalling new mire

indicators.note: divergent says the plural ways split up, one street landing in one place and the other elsewhere
landing in something means ending up inside it, so these letters are put inside
appalling means dreadful, so the letters of new mire are mangled

parts.note: ways are streets, ST each; the plural supplies two of them

explanation.surface: Parliament keeps going different ways and landing in a dreadful new quagmire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appalling' rearranges NEW MIRE as WEMINER. 'ways' is plural, two streets; 'divergent' and 'landing in' put them into separate places in that anagram. 'has' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Westminster is the seat of the UK Parliament and stands for it by metonymy.

clue.text: Spot of telepathy required to contact the unknown

indicators.note: one piece made to contact another is placed right against it

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, covers telepathy
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A dash of mind-reading is needed to reach out to the spirit world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'required' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, which is to spot.

clue.text: Pan's behind?

parts.note: pan means criticise harshly, and the 's of Pan's followed by behind, meaning late, spells the word too

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about the god Pan's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: To pan a show is to criticise it. Read as letters, the S of 'Pan's' followed by a word for behind (LATE) spells the same answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate a play is to criticise it severely, just as to pan it is.

clue.text: Crater's edges not evenly distributed

indicators.note: evenly picks out the even-placed letters, the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A crater's rim is lopsided, its edges uneven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not evenly distributed' looks like a description of a ragged rim, but 'evenly distributed' takes the even letters of EDGES NOT, leaving 'not' as part of the fodder. ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dent is a hollow pressed into a surface, a small crater.

clue.text: Austria, say, is in support

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria
say signals an example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Austria is, for instance, a backer of some cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Under someone's aegis means under their protection or sponsorship, their support.

clue.text: Wine's temperature reasonable

parts.note: okay means acceptable or reasonable

explanation.surface: A wine is served at a reasonable temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine.

clue.text: Lacemaker's educated but shabby

parts.note: to tat is to make lace by hand, so a lacemaker is one who tats

explanation.surface: A lacemaker is well schooled but poorly dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattered clothes are torn and ragged, which is shabby.

clue.text: Speaker's gallant about female

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a gallant is a suitor, a wooer

explanation.surface: A chatty charmer pays court to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A woofer is the loudspeaker unit that reproduces low notes.

clue.text: Key characteristics of 1, 8, 10 and 28?

parts.note: the answers to those clues begin with the four compass directions, their principal or key features

explanation.surface: A question about the main features of four other clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The four answers start NORTH, EAST, WEST and SOUTH: the main compass directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal means chief or principal, and the four main compass directions are known by this name.

clue.text: Embedded with vanguard of Indian navy, ring back

indicators.note: the vanguard is the front of an army, so the first letter
back means the word for ring is read in reverse

parts.note: to dial is to ring on the telephone

explanation.surface: Front-line Indian naval forces call home, deeply embedded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DIAL into LAID; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlaid work is set into a surface, embedded flush with it.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing tup, maybe?

definitions.meaning: an idle, lazy person who will not work
a tup is a ram, and one that mates freely might be said to ...

explanation.walkthrough: To tup is to mate, as a ram does; the second sense reads the answer as LAY ABOUT, putting it about freely.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout is an idler who does no work, a good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Rope in lieutenant to settle song

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
to settle in is to make a home inside, so the song goes within

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: A rope is used to subdue a lieutenant so a song can be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a long noosed rope.

clue.text: Some braces no good for neck

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some neck braces are useless.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'for', which is the link joining wordplay to definition: SNOG means neck alone. The pick spans braceS NO Good.
explanation.definitionFit: To neck is slang for kissing passionately, as is to snog.

clue.text: Head off bad guy — awfully tasteless

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are scrambled
taking the head off a word drops its first letter

explanation.surface: Stop that bad guy, he is horribly vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' cuts BAD to AD; 'awfully' rearranges AD and GUY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaudy means showy and garish, lacking taste.

clue.text: Faith perhaps showing adult restraint

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
a dam is a barrier that restrains water

explanation.surface: Religious belief shows grown-up self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faith' looks like religion, but it is the surname of Adam Faith, a British 1960s pop singer; 'perhaps' marks the example. 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam is the first name of the singer Adam Faith, so Faith is one bearer of it.

clue.text: Game with facetious lord over

parts.note: lud is the jokey form of lord, as in m'lud
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A joking peer finishes a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a board game with counters moved round by dice throws.

clue.text: Leaders of Coalition reject a new fisheries measure

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Coalition leaders throw out a new policy on fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cran is an old unit for measuring fresh herring catches.

clue.text: Punishing the wrong person for computer problem?

definitions.meaning: putting an innocent to death by mistake
a bug arising while a program runs

explanation.definitionFit: Execution is both capital punishment and the running of a program, so the error can be either.

clue.text: Hunter sold a fake — one from California

indicators.note: a fake is counterfeit, so the letters are reworked into a sham arrangement

explanation.surface: A hunter sells a forgery to a Californian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' rearranges HUNTERSOLDA; the dash links.
explanation.definitionFit: A Southlander is a native of a southern region, such as Southern California.
